newsitem.title: USA: Glickman says expects to stay as U.S. Ag Secretary.
newsitem.headline: Glickman says expects to stay as U.S. Ag Secretary.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Friday he expected to remain as head of the Agriculture Department if President Bill Clinton is reelected.
"I expect so," he said in answer to a reporter's question on whether he would remain in the job.
"That's presumptionus of me to say that, but i'm having a good time here," he added.
There has been speculation among officials at the Agriculture Department that he may be seeking a more senior cabinet position in a second Clinton term.
Glickman, a former Congressman from Kansas, became Agriculture Secretary in March 1995, taking over from Mike Espy, who resigned amid allegations he accepted illegal gifts.
Glickman, who headed the House Intelligence Committee while in Congress, also said there was no basis to speculation that Clinton might ask him to replace CIA director John Deutch.
